answer.text:
Marketo behavior scoring assigns points for specific actions, each with its own point value and frequency limit:

- Attended Webcast: +40 points, scored every time [marketing/marketing-operations/marketo/_index#behavior-scoring].
- Conference Booth Visit: +20 points, scored every time [marketing/marketing-operations/marketo/_index#behavior-scoring].
- Content Syndication Downloaded: +10 points, scored once every 30 days [marketing/marketing-operations/marketo/_index#behavior-scoring].
- Gated Content - High Value (Forrester or Gartner): +50 points, scored every time [marketing/marketing-operations/marketo/_index#behavior-scoring].
- Gated Content - Medium Value: +15 points, scored every time [marketing/marketing-operations/marketo/_index#behavior-scoring].
- Inbound - Medium (inbound form, not above and excluding Startup applicants): +50 points, scored once per day [marketing/marketing-operations/marketo/_index#behavior-scoring].
- Paid Social Response: +10 points, scored every time [marketing/marketing-operations/marketo/_index#behavior-scoring].

Negative behaviors (score decay) include:
- No activity in 30 days: -10 points, once per month [marketing/marketing-operations/marketo/_index#score-decay].
- Email Hard Bounce: -20 points, once per month [marketing/marketing-operations/marketo/_index#score-decay].
- Email Unsubscribed: Score reset based on demographic score, once per month [marketing/marketing-operations/marketo/_index#score-decay].

Each behavior has a "Schedule/Flow Limit" that determines how often points can be assigned for that action (e.g., every time, once per day, once per month) [marketing/marketing-operations/marketo/_index#behavior-scoring].

You can view recent score changes and the activities that triggered them in the Marketo score tab, and cross-reference them with the scoring rubric for more details [marketing/marketing-operations/marketo/_index#score].
